parts.article:
The History of Barcodes

A Barcodes may seem common enough today that it is difficult to imagine a shopping trip without them. However, barcodes were not of much importance until the 1970s. The first product to be barcoded and scanned with the first barcode scanner ever used was in 1974. The idea of barcodes, on the other hand, is not quite as recent. In 1932, Wallace Flint suggested that it might be feasible to create an automated retail checkout system. Even though his idea was not considered practical at the time, Flint continued to support the development of automated checkouts throughout his working life. He later became a key figure in the development of the UPC code and went on to become vice-president of an association of food chains about forty years later.

B There is a common misunderstanding that the retail UPC barcode was the first barcode. In fact, the first barcode symbology was not referred to as a barcode when it was first invented. At that time, it resembled a bull’s-eye target consisting of a set of concentric circles. This design was chosen because it could be scanned from any direction, later gaining the nickname the "Bullseye barcode". Two college students, Joseph Woodland and Bernard Silver, created this design after realising that something similar was needed to track huge inventories in rapidly growing supermarkets. Woodland later joined IBM in 1951 and persuaded the company to bring in a consultant to study barcodes. As he considered the future needs of grocery stores, he based his initial idea on Morse Code. Instead of using dots and dashes, however, he lengthened them into a series of wide and narrow lines, creating the first linear barcode. This vertical pattern of lines was then arranged into a circle.

C Meanwhile, a scanner that could read these codes was also being developed. Finally, in 1952, the Bullseye code and the linear version were patented, along with the mechanical and electrical scanner systems designed to read them. IBM suggested that it buy the patent, but did not agree to match the asking price because the company did not think the product was marketable enough at that time. Philco, however, did agree to the price and later sold the patent to RCA. This event marked the beginning of a new era in automatic identification and electronics as a whole.

D It was not until 1967, when RCA started promoting the Bullseye to the grocery industry, that the code was actually used. One Kroger grocery store agreed to be the first to try the Bullseye, while RCA attempted to highlight the potential savings made possible by automating the checkout counter. However, although the Bullseye required less scanner orientation, the code occupied a large amount of space, and its circular design restricted the quantity of data that could be encoded. The Bullseye therefore needed further refinement, since the technology at that time could not yet manage variable printing effectively, and scanners were still being improved.

E At the same time, as developers were increasing the capabilities of scanning equipment and computer technology, progress in automatic identification began to focus on the railroad system that supported the retail and manufacturing industries. Freight cars often travel from one end of the country to the other, and they are sometimes borrowed by one rail line from another. As a result, tracking freight trains as they move around the country is extremely challenging.

F Barcodes were first applied in the American railroad system in the late 1960s. At that time, the Association of American Railroads introduced a system called KarTrak, designed by a railroad employee and MIT graduate named David Collins. The system used blue and red reflective stripes painted on steel plates attached to the sides of railroad cars. The plates had thirteen horizontal labels, which closely resembled barcodes. They included start labels, stop labels and check numbers. The placement of these stripes encoded a four-digit railroad company identifier as well as a six-digit car number. When railcars passed through rail yards, this information could be scanned and used to identify them.

G Around ten years later, the same program fell into disuse after an economic downturn. The system was also considered unreliable and error-prone because the stripes could become contaminated with dirt. By the 1980s, radio tags had become the dominant method of tracking railroad cars. Collins, however, still saw other possible uses for barcodes, especially in industrial settings. He went on to establish a company called Computer Identics Corporation. General Motors became one of the first companies to monitor the production and distribution of car parts using these barcodes, while another early system was used in a distribution facility.

analyses.content: Flint在1932年提出了自动结账的早期构想，但受限于当时的技术并不实用，完美对应选项i（一个尚未在技术上实用的早期提议）。
你可能会误选关于超市无线电标签的选项x，但本段并未提到无线电技术，且该提议仅仅停留在早期构想阶段。

In 1932, Wallace Flint suggested that it might be feasible to create an automated retail checkout system. Even though his idea was not considered practical at the time, Flint continued to support the development of automated checkouts throughout his working life.
段落详细描述了条形码最早的形态设计，以及它从莫斯密码的点划线逐渐改变成线条和圆形外观的过程，对应选项ii（早期代码设计在形式上是如何改变的）。
你可能会看到第一句提到条形码并非第一个而被误导，但本段的核心其实是在讲设计的演进与变化过程。

As he considered the future needs of grocery stores, he based his initial idea on Morse Code. Instead of using dots and dashes, however, he lengthened them into a series of wide and narrow lines, creating the first linear barcode. This vertical pattern of lines was then arranged into a circle.
本段讲述了扫描器和条形码被申请专利的过程，以及IBM因为觉得市场不够而错失了商业机会，对应选项iii（专利、扫描器以及错失的商业机会）。
本段虽然在句尾提到了自动识别新时代，但核心说的是专利归属和商业买卖，不要脱离了“未被把握的商业机会”这一主旨。

Finally, in 1952, the Bullseye code and the linear version were patented, along with the mechanical and electrical scanner systems designed to read them. IBM suggested that it buy the patent, but did not agree to match the asking price because the company did not think the product was marketable enough at that time.
Kroger超市首次试用了这种条形码，但也暴露出它占地方且数据量受限的设计缺陷，对应选项iv（第一次食品店试验及设计的局限性）。
你可能会因为看到“节省成本”而想选商业相关选项，但这只是试验的初衷，段落重点更在于其暴露出的设计局限性。

One Kroger grocery store agreed to be the first to try the Bullseye, while RCA attempted to highlight the potential savings made possible by automating the checkout counter. However, although the Bullseye required less scanner orientation, the code occupied a large amount of space, and its circular design restricted the quantity of data that could be encoded. The Bullseye therefore needed further refinement, since the technology at that time could not yet manage variable printing effectively, and scanners were still being improved.
段落说明了货运列车不仅跨国行驶还会被互相借用，导致追踪极其困难，这就解释了铁路行业为什么需要自动识别系统，对应选项v（为什么铁路行业需要自动识别）。
不要因为看到段首的制造和零售业就被干扰，这段的主体是说明铁路系统因为追踪困难而对该技术的渴求。

Freight cars often travel from one end of the country to the other, and they are sometimes borrowed by one rail line from another. As a result, tracking freight trains as they move around the country is extremely challenging.
段落具体介绍了条形码系统是如何被做成红蓝反光条标签，并应用在货运列车车厢侧面的，对应选项vi（将条形码式的标签应用在货车车厢上）。
你可能会选viii（首次应用在火车票上），但原文明确提到标签是贴在货运车厢上，并非火车票。
The system used blue and red reflective stripes painted on steel plates attached to the sides of railroad cars. The plates had thirteen horizontal labels, which closely resembled barcodes.
段落讲述了该系统在铁路行业因为经济衰退和污垢干扰而没落，但随后在工业和汽车制造领域得到了更广泛的应用，对应选项vii（在一个领域的衰落和在另一个领域的更广泛使用）。
这段既写了在铁路的衰落也写了在别处的新生，不要只看前半段的“停用”而忽略了后半段的大面积扩展。

Around ten years later, the same program fell into disuse after an economic downturn. The system was also considered unreliable and error-prone because the stripes could become contaminated with dirt. By the 1980s, radio tags had become the dominant method of tracking railroad cars. Collins, however, still saw other possible uses for barcodes, especially in industrial settings. He went on to establish a company called Computer Identics Corporation. General Motors became one of the first companies to monitor the production and distribution of car parts using these barcodes, while another early system was used in a distribution facility.

questions.question: Wallace Flint created the first barcode used in supermarkets.

analyses.content: Wallace Flint在1932年提出的是“自动结账系统”的构想，并没有直接发明出第一个在超市使用的条形码。
你可能会把“自动化零售结账”等同于“发明条形码”，但实际上首个条形码是后面的大学生发明的，概念不能混淆。
